blocks.text:
Buenos Aires introduces you to Argentine history, tango and European architecture. The programme includes Plaza de Mayo, La Boca and Caminito, San Telmo, Puerto Madero, Recoleta and Palermo. The city unfolds gradually, from old neighbourhoods and its port history to modern waterfronts, broad avenues and green districts.

On the Patagonian coast, you will visit Península Valdés, with southern right whales and elephant seals, and the Magellanic penguin colony at El Pedral. The vastness of the landscape is particularly striking here: open steppe stretches towards the Atlantic, and wildlife watching becomes part of the journey rather than a brief stop.

The route then heads further south to Ushuaia: Tierra del Fuego National Park, the Beagle Channel, islands with birds and sea lions, Les Eclaireurs Lighthouse, and Lakes Fagnano and Escondido. One day takes you through the forests and along the coast of the national park; on another, you set off in off-road vehicles towards the lakes, crossing streams and following remote tracks.

In El Calafate, the main attraction is the Perito Moreno Glacier in Los Glaciares National Park. You can see it from a network of viewing walkways and from the water on the Safari Náutico boat trip. A free day gives you the chance to add a separate excursion across Lago Argentino to other glaciers.

The final nature-focused part of the tour takes place in Iguazú. The programme includes the Argentine and Brazilian sides of the falls, the rainforest and viewing trails. You then return to Buenos Aires and round off the journey with a tango dinner show.
